newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares rise on new Western fund wave.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares rise on new Western fund wave.

text.p: Leading Russian shares took off in early trade on Wednesday and traders said the market could hit new records by the end of the day on Western fund allocations.
The Russian Trading System index of 22 leading shares opened slightly higher at 424.75 after Tuesday's closing of 423.87.
But traders said the market was riding the wave of a fresh influx of third quarter funds from Western investors after storming to record levels just a week ago.
Dealers saw the up trend lasting to the end of the week.

"It looked like the market was set to come off this week, but in reality there are no sellers out there," said ING Baring's chief equities trader Peter Kizenko. "We're seeing another fund inflow -- we're on the road again."
National electricity company UES rose to $0.3910 at 0830 GMT after closing on Tuesday at $0.3724, while metals producer Norilsk Nickel rose to $10.15 from an unofficial $9.65 close.
Oil companies LUKoil and Surgutneftegaz also ticked up, LUKoil to $20.97 from $20.20 and Surgutneftegaz to $1.140 from $1.095.

Kizenko said he saw new records by the end of the day, but Creditanstalt Grant director of sales Tad Berger said profit taking in New York, which he said bought actively on Tuesday, might bring prices off highs.
"I think we'll see higher levels," Berger said. "It might tick back a little from the day's highs and we might see some profit taking in New York, possibly.
But dealers said the money flow would boost prices for the next few days.
"(The rise) could easily go on to end of the week because there's a lot of money waiting to be spent," said Berger.
